Here's a compact digest of the most important distinct developments in AI training data licensing deals, content partnerships, and lawsuits from the last 14 days (August 16, 2026, to August 30, 2026):

1.  **Editorial Perfil Sues OpenAI and Microsoft for Copyright Infringement in Argentina**
    Argentine news publisher Editorial Perfil initiated legal action against OpenAI and Microsoft on August 26, 2026, in Argentina. The lawsuit alleges copyright infringement and unfair competition, claiming the tech companies used its journalistic content without permission or payment to train their AI models. This is believed to be the first Spanish-language publisher to sue these AI companies over their practices.

2.  **Round Hill Music Files $1 Billion Copyright Lawsuits Against Suno and Anthropic**
    On August 17, 2026, independent music publisher Round Hill Music filed two separate copyright lawsuits against AI firms Suno and Anthropic. The suits allege that both companies illegally trained their AI models on Round Hill's copyrighted music and lyrics by scraping content from the open web without authorization. Round Hill is seeking over $1 billion in damages and has also accused Suno of DMCA violations, naming data-scraping firm Bright Data as a co-defendant.

3.  **Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music Sue Anthropic Over "Blatant Theft" of Musical Works**
    Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music filed a major copyright lawsuit against Anthropic in a federal court in Northern California earlier this week (around August 30, 2026). The suit accuses Anthropic of "one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history," alleging the company illegally torrented, scraped, and downloaded copyrighted musical compositions, including lyrics and sheet music, on a massive scale to build its AI models. The publishers are claiming $150,000 per infringed work across tens of thousands of works, potentially leading to over a billion dollars in damages.

4.  **Google Acquires Spirit Airlines' De-identified Enterprise Data for $10 Million**
    In August 2026, Google successfully acquired Spirit Airlines' de-identified enterprise data for $10 million at a bankruptcy auction, outbidding Mercor. This acquisition marks the first public price signal for company operational data as a standalone AI asset, highlighting the increasing value of such data for AI development.

5.  **AWS and NVIDIA Announce Major Expansion of AI Infrastructure Partnership**
    Amazon Web Services (AWS) and NVIDIA announced a significant expansion of their strategic collaboration on August 26, 2026, to address the growing global demand for AI infrastructure. The plan includes deploying 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across AWS's global infrastructure in 2027-2028 and deepening their joint efforts across AI factories, CPUs, networking, open models, data processing, and robotics. This partnership aims to deliver co-engineered AI solutions to accelerate AI development.

6.  **ByteDance and Hollywood Reach Global Deal on AI Copyright Protections**
    On August 25, 2026, ByteDance and Hollywood reportedly reached a global agreement concerning AI copyright protections. While specific details of the deal are not provided in the snippet, it signifies a move towards formal arrangements between a major platform and content creators regarding AI's use of copyrighted material.

7.  **EU AI Act Transparency Obligations Become Effective**
    Starting August 2, 2026, providers and deployers of certain AI systems are required to comply with the transparency obligations outlined in Article 50 of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act. These rules mandate disclosing when users interact with an AI system and embedding machine-readable markings for AI-generated or manipulated synthetic audio, image, video, or text. Non-compliance can result in significant fines.

2. [forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/virginieberger/2026/08/26/round-hill-sues-suno-anthropic---illegally-scraped-music-isnt-fair-use/)
3. [mishcon.com](https://www.mishcon.com/generative-ai-intellectual-property-cases-and-policy-tracker)
4. [pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/news/anthropic-hit-with-new-copyright-lawsuit-from-sony-warner)
5. [troveo.ai](https://www.troveo.ai/resources/ai-training-data-statistics)
6. [nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/aws-and-nvidia-to-deliver-2-million-additional-gpus-and-next-generation-infrastructure-for-agentic-and-physical-ai)
7. [aboutamazon.com](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws-nvidia-2-million-gpus-ai)

Here is a compact digest of important developments in AI training data licensing deals, content partnerships, and lawsuits from the last 14 days:

1.  **Round Hill Music Sues Suno and Anthropic for Copyright Infringement**
    Independent music publisher Round Hill Music filed two separate copyright lawsuits on August 17, 2026, against AI firms Suno and Anthropic. The lawsuits allege that both companies illegally trained their AI models on Round Hill's copyrighted music and lyrics, including popular songs, by scraping content from the open web without permission or license. Round Hill is seeking over $1 billion in damages and has also accused Suno of Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) violations, naming data-scraping firm Bright Data as a co-defendant in the Suno suit.

2.  **Brazilian Newspaper Folha Settles Lawsuit with OpenAI and Signs Deal with Google**
    Brazilian newspaper Folha has settled its copyright lawsuit against OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, by entering into an agreement with the AI company. This settlement follows closely on the heels of Folha announcing a separate content licensing deal with Google. The specifics of both agreements were not immediately disclosed, but they represent a trend of publishers seeking compensation and control over their content used in AI training.

3.  **Microsoft Secures Content Deal with Australia's Nine Entertainment**
    Microsoft has signed its first content licensing deal for news in the Asia Pacific region with Australia's Nine Entertainment. This partnership allows Microsoft to access Nine Entertainment's content, likely for training its AI models and enhancing its AI-powered services. The terms of the agreement were not publicly disclosed.

4.  **Judge Largely Rejects Perplexity's Motion to Dismiss Reddit's Copyright Lawsuit**
    A federal judge on July 31, 2026, largely rejected an attempt by Perplexity and SerpApi to dismiss a copyright lawsuit filed by Reddit. Reddit's lawsuit, originally filed in October of the previous year, accuses Perplexity and three data-scraping suppliers (SerpApi, Oxylabs, and AWMProxy) of "industrial-scale" bypassing of technical protections to obtain Reddit content for Perplexity's AI answer engine. The judge's ruling indicates that Reddit has plausibly argued that Perplexity conspired with at least one of the data scrapers to bypass access controls and acquire Reddit's material.

2. [pressgazette.co.uk](https://pressgazette.co.uk/platforms/news-publisher-ai-deals-lawsuits-openai-google/)
